grh_7ffcc2dbbf0563b6ac31.title: Apartment in Athens
paragraphs: In occupied Athens, Nicholas Helianos deliberately takes a German officer, Captain Kalter, into his family home in hopes that apparent cooperation will protect them. The arrangement humiliates his wife Zoe and son Alex, while Kalter dominates the household and the family learns how dangerous even small acts of resistance can be. After a trip home, Kalter returns shattered by the deaths of his wife and son. Nicholas briefly sympathizes with him, then condemns the leaders who caused both Greek and German suffering. Kalter responds by summoning the military police. Facing execution, Nicholas sends Alex to join relatives in the mountains and leaves him one final lesson: never trust the occupier.

This [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] broadcast aired on April 10, 1945. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Ronnie Liss, Wendell Holmes, Peter Capell, Betty Kane, and Jean Elkins. Other credited names include Phyllis Parker as radio adaptor.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.69c3e4b6c63c9509|Apartment in Athens]]. Glenway Wescott is credited as author and Phyllis Parker adapted it for radio.

grh_7f6089e293e4dbd58cbd.title: A Scandal in Bohemia
paragraphs: The King of Bohemia hires Holmes to recover a compromising photograph of himself with Irene Adler before it can threaten his forthcoming marriage. Disguised as a clergyman, Holmes stages a street disturbance and false fire alarm to make Irene reveal where she keeps the photograph. Irene recognizes him, however, follows him in disguise and leaves England with her new husband, Godfrey Norton. She takes the incriminating photograph with her but promises never to use it against the king, leaving Holmes a different portrait and the lasting memory of the woman who outwitted him.

[[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Basil Rathbone and Nigel Bruce. Other credited names include Edna Best as producer, Anthony Boucher as radio adaptor, Denis Green as radio adaptor, and Harry Bartell as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]] and [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]].

grh_7f430bb6fc15125e84f4.title: Johnny Stringer
paragraphs: After a hotelkeeper is shot, Britt and the sheriff follow the trail of notorious gunman Johnny Stringer to a young woman named Maria, who has been hiding a man she knows under an alias and expects to marry. The lawmen reveal that her guest is Stringer, already married and accustomed to using women to help him escape. When Stringer turns a gun on Britt and the sheriff, Maria accepts that she has been deceived and kills him with a knife. Britt later argues that her act may have saved their lives, and she appears to come through the legal aftermath safely.

grh_7fedb17d338c41167e4d.title: The Odyssey of Number Fourteen
paragraphs: A reporter investigates the secret disappearance of astronaut Ted Shaw after an unexplained launch. Officials finally reveal that Shaw was sent through the Plickin radiation field, whose strange sound effects produced a kind of audio hypnosis that made him desperate to remain in orbit. Ground controllers had secretly locked him out of manual control and forced the capsule back to Earth, after which he withdrew into near-catatonia. Shaw's wife joins his rehabilitation and patiently uses familiar speech and coordination exercises until he begins responding again.

This [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]] broadcast aired on September 22, 1964. It is listed as episode 37 in the archive. [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes [[person|lon-clark|Lon Clark]]. Other credited names include Fred Foy as announcer.
